chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Walking chromatic bass lines and band resistance
summary: Players resisted his chromatic walking bass in One O'Clock Jump and his new style until the record came out and was accepted.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: It depends on who was in that band, too.
Well, the --
They had a hard time getting some of those bands like that, you know. They didn't want you to change it.
Yeah, yeah.
And the rhythm section, they didn't like the base fiddle walking too much, like One O'Clock Jump?
Right.
They said that was out of tune, out of chord, because the bass -- if it's a B flat chord, I was using everything else in there, chromatic-ing that bass, but it's
dissolving all the time, dissolving just like a train moving.
Well, I mean, that was one thing about Walter Page. He was more or less a straight or hit man in the chord, wasn't he?
Yeah, and then I started training him to working in that One O'Clock Jump.
Yeah.

And then that's when a lot of bass players resented that, when they saw it on the music. And the orchestration came out there and they had to walk where the bass can play those chromatic things. He's in a section all by hisself, just about, when he leaves the rest of the section, he can do anything, you know.
eah.
You know, take a B flat chord, consisting of B flat, G and F and D, well, I'm using an E flat in that, and E natural and F sharps and A's and chromatic for the dissolving of the tones.

Yes. Of course, some of them -- when you start to bring things like that into an old established family of older guys, I suppose some of them -- they didn't want -- they wanted to stay with what they knew.
He changed the style of the band. We're not Benny Morton's band no more.
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
We're something else. We ain't playing that style no more.
Yeah, well, I can understand that.
But after it got on the record, and the record come out, that's the only time they accepted the thing.
Yeah.
Man, the record's out, that's it. They didn't understand it, and the music (inaudible) the public.
